business_scope.primary_industry_name: Computerized Embroidery and Ultrasonic Seaming of Custom Plush Dolls

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Hispanic-Colombian heritage with strong U.S.-influenced commercial statutes)

EU–Central America Association Agreement (provisionally applied with Panama since 1 August 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Private Interest Foundations are governed by Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 as amended by Ley 9 de 2012 and Decreto Ejecutivo 83 de 2013. AML/CFT obligations are governed by Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015, Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 2 de junio de 2015, and the annual Personas Jurídicas (PPSA) beneficial-ownership filing regime administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) under the Código Fiscal. Resident agents must maintain a UBO record at their certified office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notario Público de Panamá, subsequently registered with the Registro Público de Panamá

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if origin country is not a Hague Apostille Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization; apostille by Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores if used outside Panama

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and the domestic designated-persons list published by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). Under Ley 23 de 2015, risk-based Customer Due Diligence is mandatory before incorporation: identify the founder, foundation council members, beneficiaries and ultimate beneficial owners holding at least 25% of rights, assets or control. Enhanced Due Diligence applies to foreign and domestic Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including source-of-wealth verification. The Low_Risk_Standard plush-toy OEM scope requires standard CDD with annual refresh; any sanctioned-party match triggers immediate suspension and SAR filing to the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Sistema de Reserva de Nombre en Línea (SRL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name may be in Spanish or any language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin script must be romanized as no non-Latin characters are accepted by the Public Registry. The charter must contain the statutory suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the formula 'Fundación [name]'. The registered name must be distinguishable from all existing entities; no official Spanish transliteration is required, but the exact registered spelling must match the charter and all subsequent certificates.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerio / Gobierno / Presidencia / Nacional in a manner implying official status
Substantially identical or confusingly similar names already registered
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the preferred name is rejected, file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Dirección General del Registro Público within 5 business days, annexing the rejection certificate and arguments of visual and phonetic distinctiveness. If denied, an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) lies within 60 calendar days for review by the Civil Law Chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. In parallel, reserve two or three alternative names online before the expiry of the original reservation to preserve the incorporation calendar. The 30-day reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30-day term by timely filing a new MR-810 application before lapse; expired reservations return to the first-come pool.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this passive asset-holding PIF. The foundation must appoint a resident agent (abogado idóneo) maintaining a physical Panama office that serves as the registered office and holds statutory books, UBO records, and AML files. A virtual office is accepted for the foundation itself provided the resident agent's physical presence satisfies the registered-office mandate; the low-risk export-oriented plush-toy OEM business may operate remotely without Panama situs activities while preserving territorial tax neutrality.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 15% probability of unannounced inspection within the first 12 months, driven principally by UAF supervision of the resident agent and registered-office holder under the DNFBP framework. Direct inspection of the foundation for a license-free Low_Risk_Standard toy OEM is below 5%, rising only upon PEP triggers, sanctioned-party hits, atypical transaction flows, or inconsistency between declared UBO data and public-source reporting.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Private Interest Foundation Law (Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995), as amended by Law 61 of 2015 and Law 13 of 2017; specifically Articles 1-4 (constitution), 7 (initial endowment), 18-20 (foundation council), and 35-38 (registration with the Public Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General del Registro, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, General Registry Directorate, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter executed as a Public Deed (Acta de Constitución / Escritura de Fundación de Interés Privado) before a Panamanian Notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment of at least USD 10,000 (B/.10,000) or equivalent assets. No mandatory escrow deposit or proof of blocked funds is required at registration, but the endowment assets must be identified in the charter and accepted by the first Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the organizers of the Private Interest Foundation approve and accept the Foundation Charter and the initial endowment of US$10,000, declared per Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Foundation be established at [Street Address, City of Panama, Republic of Panama], and the registered agent be appointed accordingly. RESOLVED, that the members of the Foundation Council be appointed to serve as guardians of the foundation’s assets, with full powers to manage investments, execute contracts, and comply with lawful instructions of the protector. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts and to initiate registration in the Public Registry of Panama.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Instituto de Nombres (Name Clearing Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application to the Public Registry's name reservation system. The proposed foundation name must include 'Fundación' or a permitted abbreviation such as 'P.F.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registrant. Upon clearance, obtain the Name Reservation Certificate before drafting any deed.
required_dossiers: Official name reservation application form (Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre)
Copy of the founder's passport or national ID
Power of attorney if the filing is submitted through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused due to similarity, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the Name Clearing Office within 15 business days or submit an amended name application; the first re-submission is exempt from an additional search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Circuito (Panama Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the draft Foundation Charter and optional Foundation Regulations to a Panamanian notary. The notary verifies the inclusion of the foundation name, registered office, initial endowment, Foundation Council members, protector (if any), and resident agent. The founder and initial council members must physically appear or be represented under an authenticated power of attorney. The notary records the act in the protocol book and issues a certified copy for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter and Foundation Regulations (Reglamento)
Original Name Reservation Certificate issued by the Public Registry
Passport copies of the founder, foundation council members, and protector (if any)
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or ownership title)
Letter of acceptance from the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the draft because of insufficient asset identification or prohibited purposes, the charter is amended and re-executed in a new notarial act; notarial annotations may be corrected using a private document amendment presented to the same notary without losing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration before the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first certified copy of the constitutional deed with the Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado. The registry examines compliance with Law 25 of 1995, assesses the official registration fee, and upon approval assigns an entry number and inscription folio. The foundation acquires legal personality only after this registration is perfected.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter deed (Testimonio)
Proof of payment of the registration fee (B/.250)
Two photocopies of the notarial deed for the registry file and stamping return
Written acceptance of the resident agent appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a complement of requirements ('causales'), the applicant must file the missing documentation within five business days. If substantive corrections are required, a corrective deed must be executed before the same notary and resubmitted. An aggrieved applicant may appeal to the Director General of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Foundation Council Meeting and Post-Registration Ratification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council and Resident Agent; registered office administration under the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the Foundation Council to adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, approve the acceptance of the initial endowment, confirm the registered office, and appoint the council officers. The minutes shall be recorded in the foundation minute book and signed by the council members. After this step, the foundation may proceed to obtain tax identification (RUC) and industrial operating permits before commencing any manufacturing activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate and folio number issued by the Public Registry
Minutes and written resolutions of the first Foundation Council meeting
Statutory minute book (libro de actas) for foundation acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the council meeting is challenged for lack of proper convening, the council must hold a second validated session with strict notice compliance. If the resident agent refuses to complete sworn filings, the foundation may replace the resident agent through an additional registered deed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Regulación y Registro Industrial; and Municipio de Panamá (Municipality of Panama) for the municipal Aviso de Operación
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Industrial (Industrial Operation Notice) accompanied by the MICI Industrial Registry Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Registration and Environmental Compliance Report (Informe Ambiental de Cumplimiento), applicable to low-impact ultrasonic seaming and computerized embroidery of stuffed toys; a full EIA may be required if the facility is located near protected areas or exceeds MiAMBIENTE production thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet Executive Decree No. 4 of 2002 effluent standards, including maximum BOD5 of 100 mg/L, COD of 200 mg/L, TSS of 100 mg/L, and pH between 6 and 9. Atmospheric VOC emissions from ultrasonic welding and adhesive use must remain below the limits set by MiAMBIENTE air quality regulations, with local extraction and carbon filtration installed where fugitive emissions are detected. Textile offcuts, adhesive containers, and dye residue must be segregated for permitted municipal or authorized industrial waste handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load report verifying floor loading capacity for embroidery and ultrasonic sealing machinery; occupational health clearance from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) and workplace safety review by the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), covering lighting, noise, ergonomics, and emergency evacuation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online services portal: Sede Electrónica (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa) and Electronic Invoicing System (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), the resident agent and the foundation's designated representative must apply to the DGI for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC). The application is filed through the Sede Electrónica portal using the foundation's public deed and proof of appointment of the resident agent. The DGI issues a permanent RUC number (NIT) and registers the PIF as a territorial taxpayer. Foreign ownership does not require local presence beyond the resident agent, and the RUC application may be completed remotely with apostilled documents and a power of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box regime. A PIF may elect to be treated as an active business taxpayer for Panamanian-source activities (thus subject to local income tax and ITBMS), or as a passive foreign-source income vehicle that is not subject to Panamanian income tax on non-Panamanian income. Hybrid mismatch elections are not statutorily available under Panamanian domestic law, but treaty and BEPS-consistent alignment may apply for cross-border payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — VAT-equivalent transfer tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No single numeric registration threshold for business entities; all persons engaged in commercial activities in Panama must obtain a RUC. Small taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding PAB 36,000 (effectively USD 36,000) may apply for a simplified ITBMS payment method, while full registration and monthly/quarterly filing apply above this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taxpayers authorized by the DGI must issue electronic invoices through the Facturación Electrónica de Panamá platform. The system requires real-time transmission of invoice data to the DGI, use of a DGI-authorized digital stamp (QR code with a unique validation code), and compliance with API integration rules. Foreign-owned exporters must use certified software or the free DGI web portal to file/report invoices; no separate pre-clearance of each invoice is generally required except for high-risk taxpayers, but data must be transmitted promptly upon issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% ITBMS applies to (i) the sale of movable goods physically exported from Panama, (ii) services rendered to non-resident persons for use or enjoyment entirely outside Panama, (iii) international transport of goods or persons, and (iv) goods and services supplied to duty-free zones or international transit regimes. The exporter must retain documentary evidence that the goods left Panamanian territory and were received abroad, and that payment was received from a non-resident or from export proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment to the foreign buyer
Commercial Invoice issued by the Panamanian entity with a clear description of plush toys (ISIC 3240)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer proof showing settlement of the export proceeds from a foreign bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and Customs Authority may retroactively audit zero-rated export transactions for up to five fiscal years. If documentation is incomplete, fraudulent, or the goods are deemed to have been consumed domestically, the taxpayer is liable for the uncollected 7% ITBMS plus applicable surcharges, late payment interest, and fines of up to 200% of the omitted tax per the Fiscal Code. Criminal penalties, including imprisonment, may apply for false declarations, forged bills of lading, or fictitious export operations designed to obtain refunds or zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — Panama has no issuing central bank; the US dollar circulates as legal tender alongside the balboa (fixed 1:1) under Law 84 of 1941, and the SBP exercises banking supervision and prudential regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system with zero exchange controls; capital and current account transactions are freely convertible, with no quotas, approvals, or profit-remittance barriers for a Private Interest Foundation (PIF). Dividends, capital withdrawals, and trade payments may be remitted without central bank authorization; the sole friction is bank-level AML/CFT compliance pursuant to Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Acuerdo 4 de 2016.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender, conversion window, or repatriation ratio on export receipts; proceeds from the sale of plush mascots may be retained in any jurisdiction or currency as determined by the foundation council.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and segregated USD trade settlement sub-accounts
Capital Escrow Account for PIF endowment and reserve funds
Operational Account and Documentary Letter of Credit issuing desk
Operational Account for low-ticket OEM and platform disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with material legal constraints. Panama regulates fintech firms under Law 174 of 2020 and crypto businesses under Law 697 of 2023, but offshore digital EMIs are not licensed as Panamanian payment institutions; they may service the PIF only through bank-backed partnership rails or a local fintech registration. EMI accounts are acceptable for platform payouts and small USD flows, but are not accepted as the primary treasury rail for LC-backed or high-value OEM trade settlements because tier-1 originating banks require a clean bank-to-bank transfer trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for at least the Foundation Council president or a formally appointed delegate holding notarized powers; remote account opening is permitted only where the founders complete sworn declarations before a Panamanian consul or a notary at the Registro Público, followed by a live video verification which supplements rather than replaces initial due diligence. SBP AML rules require identification of all beneficial owners and a documented in-person or consular-verified interview for non-resident PIFs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity — will-holder, protector, and foundation council are considered non-equivalent to corporate directors; the account may be classified as high-risk shell structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certified copy of the Pacto Fundacional and Reglamento; Registro de Beneficiarios Finales certificate; sworn declaration that no bearer shares or coded instruments exist; full beneficial-ownership chart; foundation council resolutions appointing the account signatories; valid foundation Good Standing certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of the initial foundation endowment or capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Founder's audited financial statements; 12-month original bank statements from the funding account; notarized endowment deed detailing the USD 10,000 minimum capital and subsequent contributions; underlying sales contract or invoice for the plush-toy business; proof of tax paid in the founder's residence jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance — the PIF is founded but shows no real commercial activity in Panama.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master OEM supply agreement with the plush-toy factory; Panama warehouse lease or BPO/service contract; payroll or social security records for any Panamanian staff; purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, and transport documents evidencing the physical trade flow; anticipated LCs and bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media exposure of beneficiaries, council members, or trading counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies; police clearance certificates from the country of residence; professional and bank references; negative results from World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent sanctions screening; sworn statement of no commercial nexus with sanctioned jurisdictions; official list of final buyers in verified jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 credit to the PIF's USD account at a tier-1 SBP-licensed bank; treaty purpose field (Tag 70) must state 'capital endowment of Private Interest Foundation' and reference the PIF's RUC; the sending account must be in the founder's name, and the receiving bank requires the endowment deed, foundation council resolution, and source-of-funds evidence pre-credit. For regular operating capital from a related trading entity, the rail is a documented intercompany loan or equity contribution with a signed settlement agreement and interest schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 via an SBP-licensed bank to the factory's USD or EUR account for advance payments and consignment balances; Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) issued by Banco General or Global Bank for purchase orders above USD 100,000, with Panama as the issuing jurisdiction and the factory's bank as advising/confirming bank; platform payout rails (US ACH via bank correspondent, PayPal, or Payoneer) for direct-to-consumer sales; same-day USD clearing is achieved through the US Fedwire/CHIPS correspondent network because the balboa has no independent clearing system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/GBP deliverable forwards up to 12 months quotable by Banco General and Global Bank treasury desks
USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through US or London bank desks, legally permissible because the CNY is not a fully convertible offshore currency
USD/CNH deliverable forwards or spots using the offshore yuan, where a balanced account exists with the supplier
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) available if notional exceeds USD 1,000,000 and the PIF's Reglamento expressly authorizes derivative usage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Declaration and Payment (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January of each calendar year; no anniversary extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on late payment; denial of good-standing certificates; three consecutive unpaid years justify administrative strike-off by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Anual de Renta – ISR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year-end (within three months); nil return required if no Panama-source income and the tax ID remains active
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing surcharge of 2% up to 25% of tax due, plus late-payment interest; tax clearance certificate suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección Nacional de Beneficiarios Finales (DNBF), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing under Law 261 of 2022, within the DNBF calendar window; any beneficial ownership change must be updated within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late or false filing; repeat non-compliance escalates penalties and suspends the foundation's good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent audit is mandatory for a Panama Private Interest Foundation that does not engage in Panama commercial activities. A statutory audit is triggered when the foundation's Panama-source gross annual income exceeds the DGI audit threshold (currently USD 1,000,000), or auditing is required by the foundation charter, regulations, resident agent, lender, or investor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Panama GAAP accepted. Accounting records must reflect the foundation's transactions; IFRS is required for audited financial statements in cross-border financing or tax due diligence contexts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 261 of 2022, the resident agent must confirm and electronically declare the ultimate beneficial owners each year. This protocol covers founders, foundation council members, protectors, and beneficiaries, including rights arising from any foundation-interest transfer. The resident agent must also file an update within 30 days of any change; records must be maintained for at least 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter (Escritura de Constitución) and Regulations
Register of Foundation Council Members and Beneficiaries (if established in the regulations)
Minutes Book of the Foundation Council (Libro de Actas del Consejo de Fundación)
Accounting Books (Libros de Contabilidad) if commercial activities are carried out
